messages.subject: Found solution to start the latest R + Rattle on Debian (Squeeze) !!!
messages.subject_clean: Found solution to start the latest R + Rattle on Debian (Squeeze) !!!
messages.body_plain:
Finally after endless attempts I have found solution to this problem !!!
You need to do the following steps in this *exact order* and *every time* you start R:

> rm(list=ls())
> library(rattle)
Rattle: A free graphical interface for data mining with R.
Version 2.6.26 r55 Copyright (c) 2006-2013 Togaware Pty Ltd.
Type 'rattle()' to shake, rattle, and roll your data.
> crv$rattleUI <- "rattle_macosx.ui"
> rattle()

The good news is that once you are in running  R environment, you can exit and start rattle() many times, to your hart content, without resetting ui variable.
But once you exit R, you need to repeat the above steps within new R session.

Uff.......

Attempting to load the environment ‘package:rattle’

But, I leave it to you to track down how I did it … I don’t remember.

Bob

messages.body_plain:
The "rm(list=ls())" is needed because you would have saved the R workspace on exiting R - and that workspace is automatically reloaded when you start R next time. Unfortunately, some saved objects interfered with Rattle causing the issues you saw I think (though later versions of Rattle have attempted to rectify that and no longer saves ponjects in the user workspace). Never saving the default workspace avoids the problem (as does removing the workspace when you start up R as in your rm() command).

The use of rattle_macosx.ui is a mystery. That was an old GUI to get around some Mac OS/X bugs that I believe have now been fixed. I'm not sure what the problem could be - do you still need that after cleaning out your workspace? What happens if you don't do that step?

Graham Williams
http://togaware.com

messages.subject: Re: Graphics problem
messages.body_plain:
Hi Kennen,

This sounds like a non-rattle specific problem given the issues with Plot Builder and GGobi.

I assume you are on MS/Windows? Are you using the latest version of R (2.15.2) and Rattle (2.6.26)?

The XML dll for R gets installed when you install the XML package in R:

> install.packages("XML")

If the dll is still missing then perhaps there are issues with your PATH environment variable?

Graham Williams
http://togaware.com

> source("http://onepager.togaware.com/experi.R")

You can check you have the current version:

> source("http://onepager.togaware.com/experi.R")
> str(experi)
function (form, ds, target, modeller, details = "", n = 100, control = NULL,
    keep = FALSE, prob = "prob", class = "class")
[...]

You should see "keep = FALSE" in the correct version rather than "keep.pr <http://keep.pr> = FALSE" of the old version.

Graham Williams

messages.subject: Re: Cluster Analysis
messages.body_plain:
Hi John,

After building the hierarchical cluster simply go to the Evaluate tab and choose Score (it will be the default) and choose the Train dataset and click Execute. This will identify cluster membership for each observation and save to CSV file. You can then look at the Log tab to see the R code to see how the clusters are assigned to the observations, if you want to do something further in R, or else load the just saved CSV file in Rattle if you want to predict cluster membership, for example, using decision trees.

messages.subject: Re: SQL schema ignored in ODBC DSN
messages.subject_clean: SQL schema ignored in ODBC DSN
messages.body_plain:
I've probably not got all the possible combinations for all of the types of databases working correctly in Rattle for every case yet.

As a work-around, copy the command out of the log and paste it into the console, then add the schema and save the result into "ds" for example (rather than crs$dataset). Then choose to load ds as an R Dataset into Rattle.

Hope that helps.

Graham Williams
http://togaware.com

messages.body_plain:
There is an issue with loading projects in the current release of Rattle.

Projects can still be loaded in older releases.

It is under investigation - it arose with the recent move to ensure variables are not global - some fine tuning is required on restoring a project.

Regards,
